AGBO Executives Argue AI Will Augment, Not Replace, Human Creativity in Filmmaking

01 Nov 2026, 11:48 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: variety.com

2 min read

Key takeaways

Keynote at TIFFCOM

At the Tokyo International Film Festival’s content market (TIFFCOM), executives from the production company AGBO, founded by Anthony and Joe Russo, discussed the evolving role of artificial intelligence in the film industry. Chris Brearton, a partner at AGBO, and Dominic Hughes, the company’s chief scientific officer, emphasized that technology should serve to empower human creators rather than substitute for them.

Human-Centric Innovation

During the session, the speakers outlined several perspectives on how AI fits into their production philosophy:

  • Efficiency Over Replacement: The executives argued that AI is best suited for process efficiencies and administrative tasks that typically slow down creative workflows, rather than core creative generation.
  • Supportive Role: Drawing parallels to Pixar’s early use of 3D rendering, Hughes suggested that AI should function as a tool to help artists achieve their visions, maintaining a human-in-the-loop requirement to ensure quality and intent.
  • Limitations of AI: Hughes noted that while AI excels at data analysis and critiquing existing works, it struggles with genuine novelty. He characterized AI-generated creative writing as lacking the sophistication of a seasoned human author.
  • Commitment to Copyright: Addressing concerns regarding data usage, Brearton stated that AGBO maintains strict tracking of all AI tools used in their productions to ensure proper copyright management and transparency.

The Future of Storytelling

Brearton highlighted the concept of “concurrence”—the way modern audiences consume multiple forms of media simultaneously. He argued that the future of the industry lies in building rich, immersive worlds that can sustain audience engagement across various platforms at once. Despite the shifting technological landscape, the executives maintained that the core requirement for successful entertainment remains the ability to craft compelling stories with relatable characters.

Verification and Context

To verify these statements, readers can consult the official recordings or summaries provided by the Tokyo International Film Festival (TIFFCOM) organization. AGBO, based in Los Angeles, has produced films such as "Everything Everywhere All at Once" and the "Extraction" series. The discussion was moderated by Variety’s Asia Editor, Naman Ramachandran.
